independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: I re-derived numbering, span and every quote independently. web_mt_offset_map.json gives Ps 72 rule identity with web_title true and mt_title_verses empty, and the device inventory's superscriptions entry for 72 records mt_title_verses as prefix_of_v1 - so the claim that the li-Shlomo title sits inside MT verse 1 is correct, and the web:Ps.72.0 = oshb:Ps.72.1 form is the owner-ruled title pseudo-ref, not a defect. Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier against their cited refs (oshb:Ps.72.1 and oshb:Ps.72.4) and the WEB quotation is verbatim. The device_notes count holds: an independent skeleton sweep of the title token returns 2 verses book-wide, MT 72:1 and MT 127:1, and genre_label_membership li_shlomo is [72, 127]. The seam holds too - oshb:Ps.72.4 closes a 3ms chain and oshb:Ps.72.5 opens on a 3mp verb - and the cluster tiles Ps.72.1-Ps.72.20 exactly, 20 of 20 verses, no gap or overlap. What I contest is not the span but two factual claims about pointed 2ms suffixes, each contradicted by the row's own adjacent WEB quotation. Both share one cause: the row twice reassigns to the king a suffix that marks God, so the cure is a single reading pass over the 2ms forms of verse 1 and verse 5. Observed, not filed: the rationale ends by calling verse 5 the place where this strophe ends, though verse 5 lies outside the span and is where the next begins.

challenges.claim: The row glosses the 3mp verb at oshb:Ps.72.5 as the peoples who fear him, but that verb carries a 2ms object suffix addressing God, not a 3ms suffix referring to the king.
challenges.evidence: Byte-true from verse_map_oshb, collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.72.5: יִֽירָא֥וּךָ - the terminal suffix is 2ms, 'they shall fear YOU'. The addressee is fixed as God by the vocative and the two 2ms suffixes in the psalm's first verse, all collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.72.1: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים, מִ֭שְׁפָּטֶיךָ, וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥. Both witnesses render 2ms: “They shall fear you while the sun endures; and as long as the moon, throughout all generations.” (web:Ps.72.5) The row's own observed_substrate_signals correctly calls oshb:Ps.72.5 a 3mp verb, so the person/number analysis driving the seam is sound and only the referent gloss is wrong. Secondary: verse 5 supplies no plural subject noun at all, so 'the peoples' is an interpretive supply rather than a byte fact.

challenges.claim: The row describes the petition at oshb:Ps.72.1 as asking God for the king's own justice, but the noun carries a 2ms suffix that makes the justice God's, given to the king.
challenges.evidence: Collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.72.1: מִ֭שְׁפָּטֶיךָ is 'your judgments', 2ms, i.e. the addressee's, paired with וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ and governed by the imperative תֵּ֑ן. The row's own quotation in the same sentence contradicts the gloss: “God, give the king your justice; your righteousness to the royal son.” (web:Ps.72.1) The justice is the addressee's and is transferred to the king by the imperative; calling it the king's own inverts the possessive the pointed suffix carries.

reviews.reasoning: The row's two boundary drivers are real and byte-checkable: oshb:Ps.72.5 opens on a 3mp verb where oshb:Ps.72.4 closed a 3ms chain, and oshb:Ps.72.12 opens on a causal particle. The pointed quotes all collate at byte tier against their cited refs, and the sea-to-sea phrase correctly reflects the maqaf-free staged extract - it carries a space, not U+05BE - which shows it was spliced rather than retyped. Both WEB quotations are verbatim. The device_notes inclusio is genuine: a skeleton sweep of the two-word phrase returns 9 verses book-wide, of which exactly 2 fall in this psalm, MT 72:11 and MT 72:17. Ps 72 is an identity psalm so no dual-cite is owed; the psalm carries no selah and the row correctly claims none; and pmarks records paseq at MT 72:1, 72:4, 72:16, 72:18 and 72:19 without the row asserting any, which is correct handling of a seg-layer object. My challenges fall on the rejected_alternative, the field carrying the mandated rival disclosure: its stated ground misdescribes its own anchor verse, and it does not engage the byte-level lexical envelope that is the real case for the split it rejects.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative rejects the 5-7 / 8-11 split on the ground that both stretches share a description of the king begun at verse 5, but the verb at oshb:Ps.72.5 addresses God in the 2ms and so is not a description of the king.
challenges.evidence: Collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.72.5: יִֽירָא֥וּךָ - a 3mp verb carrying a 2ms object suffix, rendered “They shall fear you while the sun endures; and as long as the moon, throughout all generations.” (web:Ps.72.5) The row's own rationale renders the same token as 'they shall fear you', so two fields of one row disagree about one byte string. Third-person description of the king resumes at oshb:Ps.72.6, not at verse 5, so the stated ground is defective precisely at the verse it anchors on. The same sentence additionally labels the yiqtol chain 'future-tense'; the staged extract carries no morphology layer, and tense is not the byte-arguable category here - person and number are.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative dismisses the 5-7 / 8-11 split without addressing the byte-level lexical envelope bracketing 5-7, which is the strongest tier-1 warrant for the rival it disclosed.
challenges.evidence: A skeleton sweep of the lexeme returns 10 verses book-wide, of which exactly 2 lie in this psalm: MT 72:5 and MT 72:7. Both are byte-true at collate tier byte - יָ֝רֵ֗חַ closes oshb:Ps.72.5 and יָרֵֽחַ closes oshb:Ps.72.7 - bracketing the perpetuity theme: “In his days, the righteous shall flourish, and abundance of peace, until the moon is no more.” (web:Ps.72.7) Verse 8 then pivots from temporal to spatial, opening with וְ֭יֵרְדְּ (collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.72.8): “He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.” (web:Ps.72.8) The row's stated ground, shared verb person, does not distinguish 5-11 from the whole of 2-17 and so cannot carry the rejection against a repeated-lexeme envelope closing at 7. I am not asserting the span must be split; I contest a rival disclosure that rejects the split on evidence weaker than the evidence it left unaddressed.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative cites the causal particle in unpointed consonantal form while the same row cites it pointed elsewhere, leaving a skeleton-tier citation unlabeled as such.
challenges.evidence: The rationale and observed_substrate_signals carry the pointed form at collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.72.12: כִּֽי. The bare consonantal form in the rejected_alternative collates at tier skeleton against that same ref (collate.py, oshb:Ps.72.12). Campaign convention makes only byte quotation-grade for pointed text and requires skeleton or accent_stripped citations to be labeled as such in prose; this one carries no label, and the tier mismatch sits inside a single row.

reviews.reasoning: The span is sound and its drivers verify. The causal particle and the verb following it both collate at byte tier against oshb:Ps.72.12, and the jussive opening oshb:Ps.72.15 collates at byte tier, so the clause-type contrast the row uses to close at 14 is byte-grounded rather than asserted. The jussive reading is defensible from the pointed bytes - the short form against the long imperfect - which is the route available, since the staged extract carries no morphology layer. Both WEB fragments are verbatim, refs mirror cleanly including the out-of-span citation of oshb:Ps.72.15, and the psalm-level divine-name figures match yhwh_elohim_per_psalm for 72 exactly, which records yhwh 1 and elohim 2. The defect is confined to the book-level parenthetical, which renames the unit and mis-scopes the figure in one clause. Observed, not filed: the rationale spells the form label 'jussile' where the row's own rejected_alternative spells it correctly - a copy defect shared with the row across the 14|15 seam and curable in one edit.

challenges.claim: The Elohistic parenthetical misnames the count unit as verses and mis-scopes 165 as book-wide, when the inventory records both figures as Book II token counts.
challenges.evidence: psalm_device_inventory.json five_books entry II is {"psalms": "42-72", "yhwh": 32, "elohim": 165} - Book II figures. Summing five_books across I-V gives Psalter-wide totals of yhwh 695 and elohim 242, so 165 is not a book-wide elohim count; 242 is, and the row is out by 77. The toolkit declares these figures token counts of the unsuffixed noun forms, inseparable-prefixed tokens included and suffixed or short forms excluded, and directs that the object be named whenever they are cited; the row instead labels 32 as a verse count. That is two digit-bearing errors in one parenthetical - wrong unit, tokens reported as verses, and wrong scope, Book II reported as book-wide - both attributed in-field to the device inventory.

reviews.reasoning: The span's own evidence checks out. The jussive opening collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.72.15, both WEB quotations are verbatim including the elided quotation at web:Ps.72.17, and the inclusio the row builds is real: a skeleton sweep of the two-word phrase returns 9 verses book-wide with exactly 2 in this psalm, MT 72:11 and MT 72:17, so the signal's figure of 2 verses is correct and properly scoped by the refs beside it. The out-of-span citations of web:Ps.72.11 and oshb:Ps.72.18 both appear in boundary_evidence_refs, and the seam at 17|18 is formally marked on both sides - a blessing chain closing at 17, a doxology formula opening oshb:Ps.72.18. What the row omits is the disclosure duty attaching to its own closing verse: MT 72:17 is the only ketiv/qere in Psalm 72, it sits inside this span, and the row quotes and cites the verse without disclosing it. This is invisible to the machine layer - check_marks validates K/Q claims that are made and returned no flags on this cluster, so an omission cannot surface there. Observed, not filed: observed_substrate_signals spells the form label 'jussile' where the rationale spells it correctly.

challenges.claim: The row quotes and cites its span-closing verse without disclosing the ketiv/qere the inventory records there, the sole kq entry for this psalm (1 note at MT 72:17).
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json kq records exactly one entry for this psalm, Ps.72.17 with 1 note. The bytes carry the pair adjacently at MT 72:17, both at collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.72.17: ketiv ינין followed by qere יִנּ֪וֹן. The row quotes that verse and carries web:Ps.72.17 in boundary_evidence_refs, and its ellipsis elides precisely the clause that renders the pair - “His name continues as long as the sun.” (web:Ps.72.17) The inclusio anchor the row actually leans on, כָּל גּוֹיִ֥ם (collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.72.17), is untouched by the variant, so the seam and the warrant both stand; the defect is the missing disclosure on a quoted K/Q verse, not the boundary.

challenges.claim: device_notes points to another row by its unit type instead of by verse, which the register rule forbids.
challenges.evidence: The row's device_notes closes with the parenthetical pointer 'see the coda row' (straight-quoted here as row prose, per the packet convention). The standing register rule bans row-anchored and positional cross-row references outright and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored - naming the seam at 17|18 would carry the same information without leaking row structure into shipped prose. The same defect class appears on the other side of this seam, so under the seam-pair rule the cure is one edit installed on both rows.

reviews.reasoning: The span is correct and I would keep it. Its 4 Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier against their cited refs, both WEB quotations are verbatim, and the cluster tiling closes the psalm exactly at verse 20. book_ii_colophon endorses a coda span covering doxology and colophon together, so the high confidence on the span is calibrated rather than inflated - this is the one row in the cluster where high is clearly earned. The per-verse device figures are right too: book_boundary_doxologies records baruch true at both MT 72:18 and MT 72:19 and amen 2 at MT 72:19, matching the bytes בָּר֤וּךְ and וּבָר֤וּךְ, both at collate tier byte. My challenges are to the two claims the row attributes to the device inventory: one the inventory contradicts, and one that matches no object the inventory actually names.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative grounds the doxology-plus-colophon span on the device inventory tying both to one shared close, but the inventory records the colophon as a class distinct from the doxology.
challenges.evidence: psalm_device_inventory.json book_ii_colophon keys Ps.72.20 with baruch false and amen 0, and its note calls the colophon a 'tier-1 colophon class, distinct from the 72.18-19 doxology' (straight-quoted here as tool wording). The doxology entries live in a separate object, book_boundary_doxologies, which carries no entry for Ps.72.20 at all. The inventory therefore separates the two classes; what it supports is a coda span covering both, which is a different proposition from tying both into one close. The span survives on that support, but the warrant as worded asserts the opposite of its cited source, and a replacement warrant must pass the test that killed this one.

challenges.claim: The count recorded 4 times book-wide names no swept object and matches neither the inventory's entry count nor the pattern the sentence has just described.
challenges.evidence: book_boundary_doxologies holds 5 entries - Ps.41.14, Ps.72.18, Ps.72.19, Ps.89.53 and Ps.106.48 - distributed across 4 book boundaries. The clause immediately before names a 2 baruch / 2 amen pattern, and that pattern occurs at exactly 1 of those boundaries: the inventory records amen 2 at Ps.41.14, amen 0 at Ps.72.18, amen 2 at Ps.72.19, amen 2 at Ps.89.53 and amen 1 at Ps.106.48, with baruch true singly at 41, 89 and 106 and doubled only at 72. So the digit is 4 for boundaries, 5 for inventory entries and 1 for the pattern just named, and the row supplies no object to choose between them. Count-object discipline requires the swept object be named before the count is given.

challenges.claim: device_notes closes with a positional row reference, the form the register rule bans outright.
challenges.evidence: The row's device_notes ends by placing Psalm 73's opening of Book III 'on the following row' (straight-quoted here as row prose, per the packet convention). That is file-order talk of exactly the prohibited shape; the campaign rule requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored, and the seam at 72:20|73:1 carries the same content without leaking row order. The same defect class sits on the other side of this seam, so the cure is one edit across both rows.
